## Passages
RESULT [continual]: OPPD 42-5 (mAP@0.5): fine-tune 7.5, ILOD/Faster-ILOD 19.6, Dynamic Y-KD 21.7, joint 24.5. SDDD 3-2 multi-step: fine-tune 8.9, Dynamic Y-KD 21.0, joint 47.5. At best it recovers 88.6% of joint training, falling to 70.6% in harder settings.
US [continual]: This is the closest agricultural and plant-species analogue we found. Even on plant imagery, incremental methods stay clearly below joint retraining. That supports keeping 'retrain on the full accepted pool' as the reference arm while the pool still fits the cluster budget (8xV100 nodes).
CORRECTION [continual]: Accepted at CVPPA'23 (ICCV workshop). OPPD 42-5 mAP@0.5: FT 7.5, ILOD/Faster-ILOD 19.6, Dynamic Y-KD 21.7, joint 24.5 (88.6%). 27-20 gives 70.6%. SDDD 3-2: FT 8.9, Y-KD 21.0, joint 47.5, but that metric is mAP@[0.5:0.95], not mAP@0.5. Note that the paper benchmarks Dynamic Y-KD (a prior method, ref
RESULT [weeds]: Dynamic Y-KD beat ILOD and Faster-ILOD on both new and old classes, but all three methods still showed catastrophic forgetting. The author attributes this to large intra-class and small inter-class variation in plant imagery.
US [weeds]: The only close evidence on incremental training for plant detection. Adding species or data in small increments without replay will forget, even with distillation, so each increment in the professor's loop should retrain with replay of the base set or use frozen-base adapters, and the check must test old classes as well as new ones.
